subject.title: [Bug] v2026.6.9 QQBot: long markdown reply is split into N independent bubbles (one per chunk), not a single message

question: Should QQBot keep the current safe split-by-default markdown delivery behavior, or accept a bounded chunk-merge policy for messages that fit under the QQBot safe byte limit?
rationale: The current code and tests intentionally split long markdown for safety, a member has said that is by design, and an open candidate PR proposes changing the user-visible delivery policy; automation should not choose that tradeoff.

options.title: Keep intentional splitting
options.body: Treat multiple QQ message bubbles for over-limit markdown as expected behavior, document the limit/tradeoff if needed, and close or decline the linked merge PR rather than changing delivery semantics.

options.title: Accept bounded merge
options.body: Resolve and review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99032 or an equivalent patch, with live QQ proof for safe-size merge behavior and overflow behavior before landing.

options.title: Design an opt-in policy
options.body: Add no code until maintainers explicitly decide whether a user/operator-controlled merge mode is worth a new configuration surface and migration/docs cost.

recommendation.title: Keep intentional splitting
recommendation.body: Treat multiple QQ message bubbles for over-limit markdown as expected behavior, document the limit/tradeoff if needed, and close or decline the linked merge PR rather than changing delivery semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: sliverp owns the strongest QQBot markdown history signal and already gave the current by-design rationale in the issue discussion.
